app.label: Apps
app.description: Software you install — subscriptions, accounts and data lock-in decide the verdict.

game.label: Games
game.description: Games you buy for one good run — gacha pulls, pay-to-win and bait ads decide the verdict.

ai.label: AI Tools
ai.description: Tools for working and asking with AI — credits, model choice, training-data defaults and editor lock-in decide the verdict. Beyond the price list, we look first at “billed from the first request” and “is the conversation used for training”.

productivity.label: Productivity · Knowledge
productivity.description: Where your notes, knowledge and tasks live, and how you get them back out.

security-utilities.label: Security · Utilities
security-utilities.description: Tools you hand things to — passwords, authentication, cloud storage. Free limits, export, incident history and end-to-end encryption decide the verdict.

internet-privacy.label: Internet · Privacy
internet-privacy.description: The window you open the web with and what it leaks — default tracker blocking, extension limits (MV3), in-house ads and bloat decide the verdict.

strategy-card.label: Strategy · Cards
strategy-card.description: Games where you combine decks, cards and turns to solve one run.

rpg.label: RPG · Collection
rpg.description: Games about collecting and raising characters — the collection structure is the monetization structure.

action-indie.label: Action · Indie
action-indie.description: Hands-on action and indie sensibility — how it feels and how it monetizes decide the verdict.

mmorpg.label: RPG · MMORPG
mmorpg.description: Large-scale multiplayer RPGs that run for years on PC — subscription, expansions and cash-shop structure decide the verdict.

mobile-strategy.label: Mobile Strategy · Defense
mobile-strategy.description: Mobile strategy and tower defense you play one-handed — paid-once and free-plus-ads models split the field.

ai-chat-research.label: Chat · Research
ai-chat-research.description: AI you ask and search with — published free limits, training-data defaults, ads and citation decide the verdict.

ai-coding.label: Development · Coding
ai-coding.description: AI that writes and fixes code — pricing transparency, freedom of model choice and editor lock-in decide the verdict.

pkm-notes.label: Notes · Knowledge
pkm-notes.description: Where your notes and knowledge live and how you retrieve them — file ownership, accounts, sync and export split the field.

task-managers.label: Tasks · Scheduling
task-managers.description: Where tasks and schedules live and how you run them — free-tier limits, subscription lock-in, export, and forced ads or accounts split the field.

password-managers.label: Password Managers
password-managers.description: Where you entrust your passwords — free sync limits, local or open-source status, export standards and security incident history split the field.

roguelike-deckbuilder.label: Deckbuilders
roguelike-deckbuilder.description: Single-player deckbuilders that build a deck and run again — complete one-time purchases sit next to partially monetized ones.

mobile-gacha-rpg.label: Mobile Gacha RPGs
mobile-gacha-rpg.description: Mobile RPGs whose revenue is character collection, gacha pulls and server competition — the arena Pharos screens first.

action-roguelike.label: Action Roguelikes
action-roguelike.description: Real-time action roguelikes where you die and dive again — complete one-time purchases sit alongside free-to-play and ad-supported ones.

metroidvania-platformer.label: Metroidvania · Platformers
metroidvania-platformer.description: 2D action that opens up as you gain abilities — mostly one-time purchases; how it feels, the difficulty curve and DLC decide the verdict.

pc-mmorpg.label: PC MMORPGs
pc-mmorpg.description: MMORPGs that eat hundreds of hours on PC — subscription, paid expansions, free-plus-cash-shop and loot boxes, side by side.

mobile-strategy-defense.label: Mobile Strategy · Defense
mobile-strategy-defense.description: Mobile tower defense and strategy — from paid-once and ad-free to ad-and-gacha monetized, compared inside one genre.

web-browsers.label: Web Browsers
web-browsers.description: The window you open the web with — default tracker and ad blocking, Manifest V3 limits, built-in crypto, shopping or AI, and open-source status split the field.

email-clients.label: Email Clients
email-clients.description: Where you read and keep mail — account and server structure (IMAP, PGP), free limits, how AI features handle data, and open source split the field.

cloud-storage.label: Cloud Storage
cloud-storage.description: Where you entrust your files — end-to-end encryption, free capacity and device limits, access or deletion risk after cancellation, and account lock-in split the field.

ai-assistants.label: AI Assistants · Search
ai-assistants.description: AI you ask and search with — transparency of free usage and model limits, training-data opt-out defaults, ads, web citations and paid lock-in split the field.

ai-coding-tools.label: AI Coding Editors · Agents
ai-coding-tools.description: Tools that write and fix code — pricing transparency (credits and limit traps), model choice or BYOK, open source and editor lock-in split the field.

app.label: App pack
app.description: Look first at subscriptions, accounts, data lock-in and heavy collection.

game.label: Game pack
game.description: Look first at gacha, pay-to-win, paywalls on progress and bait ads.

ai.description: Look first at forced ads, opaque credit traps, forced subscription or account, and dormancy. Gacha and P2W do not exist for AI tools, so they are left out of this pack.

ai_review.summary: The essence is ‘file ownership’. Pros: Markdown, plugins, graph view, local archiving. Disadvantages: The first few weeks are spent setting up the plugin, the plugin breaks in updates, mobile text selection/copying glitches (average 2.27★ across 26 reviews), and subscription price exposure at the end of onboarding are repeatedly pointed out.

personal_fit.summary: Passes the hard filter (no ads, free, active updates). However, it does not suit the taste of viewing 'time spent setting up tools' as a cost, and although Sync subscription is optional, it is in fact a paid route.

verdict.one_liner: Start free and keep the notes as your own files for life — the Markdown and plugin ecosystem is the strength; the learning curve and mobile glitches are the conditions.
reasons: All functions can be used without advertising, accounts, or fees, so it passes all hard filters.
Strengths include file ownership, plug-in ecosystem, and Markdown plain text storage. Learning curve and mobile glitches are the costs of entry.
There is a least cost path that can be used without sync. Conformance to taste (P1) does not count towards the basic decision (v0.5.0).
condition_notes: Try the route without sync (iCloud/synchronization program) first.

objective.summary: There are no ads and it is actively updated until 2026-11-18. v0.5.0 In terms of objective standards (functional completeness, ecosystem/interconnectivity, stability, security, policy/charging transparency), the page, DB, and template ecosystem and integration are top-notch. ai_review.summary: The essence (completion, modification, and explanation without interruption within the editor) operates in the widest possible environment, and the charging reform also maintained the line of 'completion is free'. Disadvantages: Large codebase context, generic proposals, and model options are tied to organizational policy.

reasons: We continue to provide 2,000 code completions per month for free.
